transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:04] Michael Rivera: Michael here.
[00:06] Sara Liu: Sara on from ML platform.
[00:08] Daniel Park: Daniel, infra.
[00:10] Priya Patel: Priya here from Redwood SE.
[00:12] Alex Chen: Great. Goal today - review last week's benchmark, talk sizing for Dedicated, autoscale policies, and agree next steps.
[02:05] Alex Chen: Sara, can you kick off with the traffic profile you sent? I pulled the 95th percentile from your CSV, looks like bursts up to ~180 concurrent sessions for peak.
[02:20] Sara Liu: Yeah that's right, our peak window is very spiky — 30 minutes at start of day, then smaller bursts throughout. We saw p95 latencies around 220ms on our infra but that's without KV cache.
[03:10] Priya Patel: Ok, good to know. On Dedicated we usually size for sustained qps and then allow burst capacity. For your profile I'd recommend reserving a baseline pool for 100 concurrent sessions and a burst policy to add extra nodes up to capacity during spikes.
[04:00] Daniel Park: Can you explain how burst capacity works? Does it spin up new GPUs or do you borrow from a shared pool?
[04:15] Priya Patel: For Redwood Dedicated we can configure two behaviors: reserved-only where we keep a set of nodes always warm; or reserved + burst where the cluster auto-provisions additional nodes from a burst pool we keep in the account. Burst nodes can take a few seconds to be ready depending on image pull and model load. We also support pre-warmed standby to reduce cold start.
[05:30] Michael Rivera: How about autoscaling thresholds — what metrics drive scale up/down?
[05:45] Priya Patel: We typically use request concurrency and token throughput as primary signals and have a latency headroom policy. Example: scale up when 80% concurrency threshold sustained for 60s; scale down after idle for 120s. Those numbers are tunable — for Novus with spikes you may want a shorter scale-up and longer scale-down to avoid oscillation.
[07:10] Sara Liu: That 60s to scale up sounds risky for sudden spikes, we want to avoid p95 going above 300ms. Is there a way to pre-emptively schedule bursts?
[07:25] Priya Patel: Yes — scheduled scaling and traffic prediction can pre-warm capacity. Also you can set a buffer (headroom) on baseline to handle short spikes. Combining a small pre-warm window with burst pool usually gets p95 under control.
[09:00] Alex Chen: From cost perspective, keeping baseline larger increases commit cost. We prepared a cost/tradeoff worksheet. Priya, can you summarize recommended baseline for the 180 concurrent peak?
[09:22] Priya Patel: Rough rule: a single A10-style node handles ~40-60 concurrent sessions depending on sequence length and model. For your model (redwood-quant-7b variant, average seq 512) I'd estimate ~45 conc per node. For 100 baseline you'd need 3 nodes (gives ~135 capacity), burst to 5 nodes covers up to ~225. So baseline of 3 nodes + burst-to-5 is a good start.
[11:00] Daniel Park: Does that assume quantized model? We had memory issues last week when running unquantized.
[11:12] Priya Patel: It assumes 4-bit quantized variant. If you use FP16 or unquantized, memory and throughput change — you'd need fewer concurrent per node. We should confirm which variant you're testing.
[12:05] Sara Liu: We're testing quant-4 now in staging.
[12:10] Priya Patel: Perfect. That aligns with the worksheet numbers.
[13:20] Michael Rivera: How fast will the burst nodes be able to serve traffic? Concern is model load time on GPU.
[13:40] Priya Patel: Two options: warm standby where the model is already loaded (faster, seconds), or cold provision which includes model load (tens of seconds to a couple minutes). Warm standby costs more. For critical 30-minute spikes I'd recommend warm standby for at least one burst node.
[15:05] Alex Chen: Let's discuss autoscale cooldowns so we don't thrash. If we scale up quickly but scale down too fast we could pay a lot for brief spikes.
[15:30] Priya Patel: Right — recommended is scale up aggressive (30s window) but scale down conservative (5-10 minutes) plus an optional minimum billed interval. You can also set a per-node minimum run time to reduce churn.
[17:00] Sara Liu: Any existing customers doing similar pattern? Curious for cost numbers.
[17:12] Alex Chen: We have a BFS client with bursty traffic — they run baseline smaller and use burst pool with warm standby; they ended up with 15% extra cost but cut p95 violations by 90%. We'll share anonymized case study.
[18:10] Daniel Park: Security question — for Dedicated, how does KMS integrate? We need BYOK and audit logs.
[18:25] Priya Patel: Dedicated supports KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM options on Private). You can bring your keys for model artifacts and logs. Audit logs are pushed to customer-controlled S3/Cloud Storage with access controls. We can schedule a security deep dive with our security engineer.
[20:00] Michael Rivera: We'll definitely want that. Also need SOC2 type II docs before pilot expansion.
[20:12] Alex Chen: We'll attach the SOC2 pack to the thread after this call.
[21:30] Sara Liu: Back to tuning — Priya you mentioned KV-cache tuning. What's the recommended TTL and miss rate tradeoffs?
[21:50] Priya Patel: For chat-heavy workloads TTL of 10-20 minutes works well; for single-shot generation lower. The cache hit gives huge token savings. In your tests we saw a 30% token saving when conversation reuse is high. We'll run a KV-cache sweep on your sample trace and return numbers.
[24:00] Alex Chen: Ok, next up is benchmark plan. We proposed a 2-hour run with ramp and synthetic spikes at 200 conc. Sara, are you comfortable running that in staging next week?
[24:20] Sara Liu: Yes we can run that Wednesday. We need the test harness config and Redwood's suggested client driver.
[24:35] Priya Patel: I'll send the harness and the scripts, plus a recommended telemetry set (token rates, p95, model load times).
[26:10] Michael Rivera: For measuring cost, can you show estimated $/1M tokens and $/hour for baseline vs burst?
[26:25] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll add cost columns in the sizing worksheet.
[27:50] Daniel Park: Any constraints on network egress or VPC peering for Dedicated in our region?
[28:05] Priya Patel: Dedicated in that region supports VPC peering and private networking; there are limits on cross-region egress which we can document. For audit we'll also provide network diagrams.
[29:40] Sara Liu: One more question on model fallbacks — if the main model hits capacity, can we fallback to a smaller model automatically?
[29:52] Priya Patel: Yes you can set policy-based routing to fallback to smaller variants to preserve latency. Redwood's router has rules by latency, cost, and region. We can configure it for automatic fallback during bursts.
[32:00] Alex Chen: Great. Let's recap action items then we'll open for any other blockers.
[32:10] Alex Chen: Actions - Redwood sends sizing worksheet, test harness, security docs; Novus runs 2-hour benchmark Wed and provides traffic CSV; Priya runs KV-cache tuning. Any additions?
[33:05] Sara Liu: Can you also provide estimated impact of pre-warmed standby vs cold on cost?
[33:20] Alex Chen: Yes we'll add a pre-warm cost line item.
[34:40] Michael Rivera: Timeline wise, if the benchmark looks good and security checks clear, we aim to expand pilot by June 9.
[34:55] Alex Chen: Sounds reasonable.
[36:00] Daniel Park: Minor note - our infra team needs the API keys and role for test run. How's credentialing?
[36:12] Priya Patel: We'll create limited-scope API keys for the pilot and rotate them daily if desired. We'll send instructions in the thread.
[37:40] Alex Chen: Any final questions?
[38:00] Sara Liu: Not from me.
[38:10] Michael Rivera: No. Thanks, everyone.
[38:20] Alex Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the worksheet and security pack.
[38:30] (meeting ends)

Summary: Discussed Dedicated sizing for Novus Finance POC. Recommendation: baseline 3 nodes (quant-4 models) with burst to 5 nodes and 1 pre-warmed standby for critical spikes. Autoscale: aggressive scale-up (30-60s) and conservative scale-down (5-10m), scheduled pre-warm for known spikes. Action items and next steps captured.

References/Links: Dedicated sizing worksheet (will be shared), test harness scripts (link to be provided), SOC2 pack (link to be provided).
